artifactReason: The researcher specified a CSV input at input/sample-players.csv and requested a runnable utility producing a summary report. A single-file Python script with stdlib only is the smallest artifact satisfying that goal. The previous attempt failed due to a relative-path bug; this version resolves the input path via __file__ making it location-independent.
constraintsAddressed: Keep scope minimal and runnable — single file, zero dependencies
Optimize for reproducible portfolio evidence — path resolved relative to script so it runs from any CWD
No UI unless explicitly requested — stdout only
Prefer local file processing over infrastructure — reads local CSV, no network calls
acceptanceChecks: Script executes without error when run from its own directory
Output includes per-position grouping with top scorer and average
Overall top scorer and average are printed
tradeoffs: Stdout only (no output file) keeps it simple; easily extended with argparse --output if needed
stdlib csv vs pandas: pandas is cleaner for aggregation but adds a dependency; 8 rows does not justify it
No CLI arguments: input path is hardcoded relative to __file__; acceptable for a portfolio demo script
